source: RP2040 Datasheet RP-008371-DS-1 (fetched this session via pip.raspberrypi.com -> pip-assets redirect) memory map; pico-sdk src/rp2040/hardware_regs/include/hardware/regs/addressmap.h (fetched and grepped this session) for exact base addresses -- VERIFIED, both agree.
acceptance_test: makes stock pico-sdk runtime_init() complete, per team-lead/rpi-soc's brief -- this is the honest bar, not 'reaches main'.

memory.name: xip_main
memory.why: flash, execute-in-place -- not itemized this deliverable, out of scope for the peripheral floor

memory.name: sio_bus
memory.why: per-core single-cycle IO bus. NOT the APB peripheral region below -- see peripherals[SIO].note and atomic_aliases_scope note.

atomic_aliases.applies_to: all peripherals except SIO -- see exclusion_set_verified below, NOT an apb-only allowlist

atomic_aliases_scope_note: RESOLVED 2026-08-24, correcting my own earlier draft. Team-lead assigned the follow-up task: verify the FULL exclusion set from the datasheet rather than assuming SIO is the only member. Answer, from the datasheet's own text (extracted with pdftotext -layout directly from the fetched PDF this session -- exact, page-cited, not the earlier PDF-summarizer-tool paraphrase): RP2040 Datasheet SS2.1.2 'Atomic Register Access', p.17, quoted verbatim: 'Most peripherals on RP2040 provide this functionality natively, and atomic writes have the same timing as normal read/write access. Some peripherals (I2C, UART, SPI and SSI) instead have this functionality added using a bus interposer, which translates upstream atomic writes into downstream read-modify-write sequences, at the boundary of the peripheral. This extends the access time by two system clock cycles. The SIO (Section 2.3.1), a single-cycle IO block attached directly to the cores' IO ports, does not support atomic accesses at the bus level, although some individual registers (e.g. GPIO) have set/clear/xor aliases.' SIO IS CONFIRMED AS THE ONLY NAMED EXCLUSION -- no other peripheral is named as lacking atomic access. THIS CORRECTS MY EARLIER 'applies_to: apb' FRAMING, which was too narrow and reasoned from an incomplete premise (SIO's base address being outside the 0x40000000-0x4006c000 APB range, which is true but not the actual rule): the datasheet's own SSI example proves address range is not the determinant -- SSI/XIP flash controller lives at 0x18000000, nowhere near APB, yet it explicitly HAS atomic access via the bus-interposer path, just 2 cycles slower. Confirmed independently from pico-sdk source this session: hw_set_bits()/hw_clear_bits() (src/rp2_common/hardware_base/include/hardware/address_mapped.h:135-147, fetched this session) are pure address-arithmetic macros with NO bus-type check (`hw_alias_check_addr` is a no-op passthrough; a disabled commented-out version would have asserted addr>=0x40000000 'to catch likely non HW pointer types' but was never enabled), and are used routinely on DMA (base 0x50000000, e.g. `hw_set_bits(&dma_hw->inte0, ...)` in hardware_dma/dma.c) and PIO (base 0x50200000+, e.g. `hw_clear_bits(&pio->sm[sm].execctrl, ...)` in hardware_pio/pio.c) -- both fetched and grepped this session, both outside the APB range, both working via the standard native-timing path per 'most peripherals... natively'. CORRECTED MECHANISM: rather than a chip-level bus-type allowlist, the correct scoping is a per-peripheral exclusion -- SIO alone carries an explicit override (see peripherals[SIO] below), everything else defaults to aliased. The 'bus' field on each peripheral entry below is retained as informational/documentary (it correctly separates SIO's genuinely different bus topology from everything else) but is NOT what gates alias application in this corrected model -- the per-peripheral override is. UART's inclusion in the I2C/UART/SPI/SSI interposer list is worth a note for cycle-accurate work: this deliverable's uart coded-model does not currently account for the +2-cycle atomic-write penalty on UART's config registers (UARTCR/UARTLCR_H/etc. if firmware used hw_set_bits on them), since this deliverable models UART at the FIFO/data-flow level where the doc's virtual-cycle determinism rule already applies -- flagged as a fidelity gap for whoever adds cycle-accurate bus timing, not a correctness gap for boot-to-blink.

peripherals.name: PLL_USB
peripherals.why: same regmap file as PLL_SYS -- SVD declares PLL_USB as derivedFrom="PLL_SYS", identical register layout, VERIFIED this session (RP2040.svd line 33800).

peripherals.name: UART0
peripherals.why: kind-8 hw per design doc SS1 point 8's own worked example -- 'UART data and FIFO flags (TXE waits are data-flow, not enable-flow; an RX read pops a FIFO)'. See coded-model-notes/rp2040_uart.json for the register facts a coded: implementation needs (TXFF/RXFE/BUSY spin targets, offsets, why-citations) -- kept as reference data even though the peripheral itself routes to code, not schema.

peripherals.name: SIO
peripherals.why: whole-peripheral kind-8 hw: GPIO pin events out (matches design doc SS3's GPIO/pin-event reasoning for why models are Python-side), CPUID is per-core identity (not a stored field so much as a constant the model returns per-instance), and OUT/OE plus their SET/CLR/XOR are write-side-effecting shadow registers -- the exact RP2040-hardware analogue of STM32 BSRR, which design doc SS1 point 8 names explicitly as 'the same idea as a dedicated register (kind 8)'. See coded-model-notes/rp2040_sio.json. `atomic_aliases: false` is the load-bearing field for this peripheral per atomic_aliases_scope_note above -- SIO is the chip's ONLY peripheral needing this override; every other entry in this list defaults to aliased (confirmed, not assumed: see the exclusion_set citation above).

peripherals.name: TIMER
peripherals.why: Added per team-lead's acceptance-test addendum (credited to rpi-soc): TIMERAWL/H are kind-7 counter, pure derivation from cm0_cycles() -- but ALARMn compare-and-raise-IRQ is a side effect the write clause routes to coded:, same shape as the design doc's own WDT example (SS1: 'write-protect registers gate writability of sibling registers, and expiry is a time-triggered global side effect attached to no access at all'). ALARM match -> cm0_set_irq() is exactly that pattern. See coded-model-notes/rp2040_timer.json. This is pico-sdk's delay()/sleep_ms() dependency the team-lead's addendum named -- NOT itself a status-bit spin, but a hang class of its own: a frozen or non-interrupting TIMER makes sleep_ms() block forever even with every register above correctly modelled.

acceptance_test_scope_notes: USB CDC (Serial/DTR) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this deliverable. Team-lead's addendum asked whether it's in scope 'don't silently assume' -- stated plainly: the minimum peripheral set given in the original brief and re-confirmed in the acceptance-test addendum is UART for stdio, not USB-CDC. Reaching `while(!Serial)` territory needs the full USB device controller (a much larger peripheral, per docs/architectures.md's own effort estimates for USB/PIO being bigger than the CPU core on RP2040) and is not itemized anywhere in this deliverable.
PIO is not itemized -- also out of scope, not part of the reset->runtime_init()->blink floor.
spin_detector_defeat_check: Team-lead's addendum (crediting the amended per-address-counter spin detector, esp-soc's ESP32-C3 alternating-register finding) asked whether any RP2040 runtime_init() spin has the two defeating shapes: (a) alternates between two DIFFERENT addresses within one wait, or (b) writes inside its own wait loop (feed-a-watchdog shape). Checked against every spin inventoried this session (RESETS.RESET_DONE, XOSC.STATUS.STABLE, PLL.CS.LOCK, CLOCKS.{CLK_REF,CLK_SYS}.SELECTED x2, CLOCKS.FC0_STATUS.{RUNNING,DONE}): NONE of them alternate between two addresses -- every one is a single `while (!(single_register & mask))` on one address, confirmed from the exact pico-sdk lines cited in each peripheral file below. FC0's RUNNING and DONE loops are two SEQUENTIAL single-address loops on the SAME register (fc->status) separated by a plain write to a different register (FC0_SRC) BETWEEN the loops, not alternating reads of two addresses WITHIN one loop -- this is a different shape from ESP32-C3's RTCCALICFG/RTCCALICFG2 alternation and does not defeat the per-address counter. NONE of them write inside the wait body either -- every loop found this session is exactly `while (cond) tight_loop_contents();` with tight_loop_contents() being a compiler-barrier no-op, not a register write. So RP2040's boot-critical spin set is entirely the 'safe' shape for the amended detector; nothing here needed re-verification against the ESP32-C3 failure mode.
